topic: Reliable and safe trustworthy software architectures

components.title: Recap: pipeline assessment criteria discussion
components.teaches: Students will briefly revisit the assessment criteria and reliability requirement mappings covered previously, clarifying any gaps through instructor-led discussion. This sets the context for deeper analysis of a multi-component project.

components.title: Defining reliability requirements for multi-component AI
components.teaches: Students will learn how to elicit and formalize reliability requirements for a system composed of multiple AI services (e.g., service-level objectives, error budgets, cascade failure policies). They will apply a template to a supplied project description.

components.title: Case study: industry AI pipeline reliability
components.teaches: Students will examine a real-world case study of an AI-native pipeline in production, focusing on how the organization defined reliability requirements, instrumented testing stages, and measured outcomes. They will analyse trade-offs made by the team.

components.title: Worked example: assessing supplied project pipeline
components.teaches: The instructor demonstrates a full assessment of the supplied multi-component software project's testing pipeline, linking each design decision to a specific reliability requirement and showing how to document justifications. Students follow the reasoning step by step.

components.title: Group activity: assess pipeline and justify
components.teaches: In small groups, students receive a different pipeline configuration for the same project and must assess it against the reliability requirements, producing a written justification for each design decision. Groups present findings for peer review.

components.title: Trade-offs: testing depth vs deployment speed
components.teaches: Students will compare the impact of increasing test coverage and rigor on deployment latency and resource consumption. They will evaluate scenarios where faster deployment may be preferred over exhaustive testing, supporting arguments with metrics.

video.description:
🚀 System Design #01 | Introduction to System Design for AI Product Engineering

In this session, we dive deep into System Design fundamentals and understand how modern software systems, cloud-native applications, data platforms, and AI products are designed to scale, perform, and operate reliably in production environments.

This hands-on session covers core system design concepts including scalability, availability, reliability, latency, throughput, architectural thinking, and the foundations required for designing real-world software systems and AI-powered applications.
